c: Genes do not tell you a person's support needs. Autistic people vary enormously in communication, independence and health needs, and no gene result predicts those for an individual.

The Swedish study followed 27,122 people diagnosed with autism between 1987 and 2009 against 2,672,185 matched controls. During follow-up, 706 autistic people (2.60%) had died compared with 0.91% of the general population (odds ratio 2.56; 95% CI 2.38-2.76). Mortality was raised for almost all diagnostic categories, with sex and general intellectual ability moderating the pattern
. The authors concluded that premature mortality was markedly increased owing to a multitude of medical conditions.
Why this belongs in a genetics series.

If a neurodevelopmental condition is associated with raised risk across many medical causes, then care cannot be organised as if the condition were only a mental-health matter. Whole-person medical care, with clear ownership, is the evidence-consistent model. The policy argument is developed in the policy section of this site.
What this evidence can tell us
Register studies show association, not cause. The mortality study is Swedish and covers diagnoses made between 1987 and 2009; care systems and diagnostic practice have changed since.
The 81% figure is a pooled estimate across countries and designs; individual studies differ.
The overlap between ADHD and autism genetics is stated here only in general terms until the source figures are verified.
Nothing here is advice about any individual's diagnosis or needs.
